characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed, coarse equiaxed fully recrystallised grains; coarsest grains of the group with strongly developed parallel twin-boundary bands.

characterization_methods.technique: chemical analysis (hydrogen by RH-444 Leco gas analyzer)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; average of five measurements

characterization_methods.key_findings: UTS 568 ± 7.0 MPa, YS 517 ± 9.0 MPa, total elongation 09 ± 2.16%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; average of three tests

comparative_performance.benchmark_process_id: AIMFC (air induction melting with flux cover)
comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Fe-9Al VIM exhibited about 9% total elongation and is the strongest alloy tabulated (UTS 568 MPa), whereas Fe-9Al AIMFC failed at very low stress levels without significant elongation (0.1% EL).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 50-kg capacity, 125-kW medium-frequency chamber vacuum induction furnace (G.C.A., USA); alumina-lined crucible of approximately 150 mm diameter and 300 mm height; soft iron pieces charged at the bottom with aluminum pieces on top; melt poured into 80-mm-diameter split cast iron molds kept inside the vacuum chamber.
80-mm-diameter VIM ingot preheated in a hearth furnace before hot forging.
Hot-forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature.
24-mm-thick sections of forged billets preheated at 1373 K for 1 h before hot rolling.

Hot rolled by 50% with 1-mm reduction in thickness per pass; samples reheated after every six rolling passes under similar conditions as preheating (1373 K/1 h); final thickness of hot-rolled plate 12 mm.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Hardness data are an average of five measurements; tensile data are an average of three tests.

grain_structure.texture: strongly developed parallel twin-boundary bands (annealing twins)

phases_present.phase_name: disordered Fe-Al solid solution (expected to exhibit short-range ordering)

structures.overall_structure: Annealed microstructure with coarse, fully recrystallised equiaxed grains; the VIM 9 wt.% Al hot-rolled plate shows the coarsest grains of the group with strongly developed parallel twin-boundary bands.

unmapped_findings: Fe-9 wt.% Al alloy is expected to exhibit short-range ordering (in contrast to Fe-7Al, which is a totally disordered solid solution) [b0009].
Fe-9Al VIM ingots were sound and completely free from microcracks as well as hydrogen gas porosity [b0018].
Fe-9Al produced by VIM exhibited excellent hot workability, in contrast to the poor hot-working response (microcracks) of Fe-9Al produced by AIMFC [b0041].
Measured composition of Fe-9Al VIM (wt.%): Al 9.10, Si 0.11, Mn 0.042, S 0.0027, C 0.014, O 0.0023, H 0.0021, N <0.001 [b0036/Table I].
It has been demonstrated that Fe-9 wt.% Al alloy can be produced by VIM only; AIM gave gas porosity and AIMFC gave microcracks [b0064].
